subproblems.title: Mass on open sets of an integer multiplicity current equals its representation measure (Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P open. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation in U (contract IMRep U n): M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable; θ : ℝ^P → ℕ Borel with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (continuous linear functionals on n-covectors) a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, such that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is an orthonormal family τ_1, …, τ_n spanning an approximate tangent space of M at x with ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all α, or ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = −α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all α. Here Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be represented by R: T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Put μ_R(A) := ∫_{M∩A} θ dHⁿ (the contract's R.measure). Then for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(T) = μ_R(W), where M_W(T) := sup{max(T(ω), 0) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT massOn) and |α| := (Σ_{1≤i_1<⋯<i_n≤P} α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of n-covectors (Simon 6.1.15, 6.2.5).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W

In that text, 'the parent' means the accepted node's own parent named in its Source line (provenance only; this split does not use that parent's declaration), and every 'sibling' it cites is also a sibling in this split under the same key.
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–768), stated there without proof; the argument is the one indicated in Remark 2.6 (properties (a), (b) of the norm) together with 2.7–2.8 (lines 243–283). Write E for the space of n-covectors on ℝ^P with the inner product ⟨α, α'⟩_E := Σ_I α(e_I) α'(e_I) (sum over increasing n-tuples I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n), e_I := (e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})); its norm is |·|. If n > P then E = 0, every n-form vanishes, so T = 0 and M_W(T) = 0, and Hⁿ = 0 on ℝ^P (Hausdorff dimension P < n), so μ_R = 0 and the claim holds. Assume n ≤ P.
1. (Algebra.) Let τ_1, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal and let A be the n×P matrix A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩. Expanding each τ_i in the standard basis, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I), where A_I is the n×n submatrix of A with columns I. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |α(τ)| ≤ |α| (Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2}, and by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = 1. Hence |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ E. The covector α_τ(v_1, …, v_n) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} satisfies α_τ(e_I) = det(A_I); hence ⟨α, α_τ⟩_E = α(τ) for every α, |α_τ| = 1 and α_τ(τ) = 1. (For n = 0 everything is trivial: α(τ) = α(∅) and |α| = |α(∅)|.)
2. (Consequences on M.) Let J : E* → E be the Riesz isomorphism (⟨α, J(η)⟩_E = η(α)) and β := J ∘ ξ, an Hⁿ⌞M-measurable E-valued map. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M we have ξ(x) = ±(α ↦ α(τ)) with τ orthonormal, so by step 1: |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ E, β(x) = ±α_τ, |β(x)| = 1 and ⟨β(x), ξ(x)⟩ = 1.
3. (Integrability.) For every compact K ⊆ U, μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞. If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), then tsupport ω is a compact subset of U and |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ (sup|ω|)·θ·1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, so the integrand is integrable and T(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R.
4. (Upper bound.) Let ω be admissible: ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1, and ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ = 0 if x ∉ W. Hence T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ_R(W), so max(T(ω), 0) ≤ μ_R(W). Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
5. (Lower bound: reduction to compact sets.) V := U ∩ W is open and μ_R(W) = μ_R(V) since M ⊆ U. V is the increasing union of the compact sets K_i := {x ∈ V : |x| ≤ i, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) ≥ 1/i} (K_i := {|x| ≤ i} if V = ℝ^P), so μ_R(V) = sup_i μ_R(K_i). It therefore suffices to prove M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η for every compact K ⊆ V and every η > 0. Fix K and η; if μ_R(K) = 0 there is nothing to prove.
6. (Open neighbourhood.) Choose δ > 0 with {x : dist(x, K) ≤ 2δ} ⊆ V. The sets O_s := {x : dist(x, K) < s}, 0 < s ≤ δ, have compact closures contained in V ⊆ U, so μ_R(O_δ) < ∞ and μ_R(O_s) ↓ μ_R(K) as s ↓ 0 (continuity from above; K is closed). Fix s ∈ (0, δ] with μ_R(O ∖ K) < η, where O := O_s.
7. (Lusin.) μ_R⌞K is a finite Borel measure on a compact metric space and β is μ_R-measurable; by Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT Chapter01/Lusin.lean) there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < η such that β|K' is continuous; by inner regularity we may also assume that |β| = 1 and ⟨β, ξ⟩ = 1 at every point of K' (these hold μ_R-a.e. by step 2).
8. (Continuous extension.) By Tietze's extension theorem (applied to the coordinates of β in a basis of E), β|K' extends to a continuous g_0 : ℝ^P → E. Let r : E → E be the radial retraction r(α) := α if |α| ≤ 1, r(α) := α/|α| otherwise (continuous, |r| ≤ 1, r = id on the closed unit ball). By Urysohn's lemma choose a continuous χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with χ = 1 on K' and tsupport χ ⊆ O compact. Put g := χ·(r ∘ g_0). Then g is continuous, tsupport g ⊆ O is compact, |g| ≤ 1 everywhere, and g = β on K'.
9. (Smoothing.) Let φ_σ (σ > 0) be a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, ∫φ_σ = 1, supported in the closed σ-ball) and g_σ := g * φ_σ (componentwise convolution). Then g_σ is C^∞, tsupport g_σ ⊆ {x : dist(x, tsupport g) ≤ σ} ⊆ O for 0 < σ < dist(tsupport g, ℝ^P ∖ O), |g_σ(x)| ≤ ∫ |g(x − y)| φ_σ(y) dy ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm), and g_σ → g uniformly as σ ↓ 0 (g is uniformly continuous). Viewed as an n-form, g_σ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (compact support in O ⊆ U) and g_σ is admissible for M_W(T) (O ⊆ V ⊆ W, |g_σ| ≤ 1).
10. (Estimate.) By steps 2–3, |T(g_σ) − ∫⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R| ≤ sup|g_σ − g|·μ_R(closure O) → 0 as σ ↓ 0. On K', ⟨g, ξ⟩ = ⟨β, ξ⟩ = 1; on O ∖ K', ⟨g, ξ⟩ ≥ −|g| ≥ −1 μ_R-a.e.; off O, g = 0. Hence ∫⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R ≥ μ_R(K') − μ_R(O ∖ K') ≥ (μ_R(K) − η) − (μ_R(O ∖ K) + μ_R(K ∖ K')) ≥ μ_R(K) − 3η. Therefore max(T(g_σ), 0) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η for σ small, and M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η.
11. By step 5, M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞); together with step 4, M_W(T) = μ_R(W). ∎
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet: for a unit simple n-vector ξ, |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm), with equality for the dual covector β = J∘ξ, |β| = 1.
Upper bound: T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ for admissible ω, so M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
Lower bound: inner regularity reduces to compact K ⊆ U ∩ W; Lusin, Tietze, radial truncation, a cut-off and mollification give smooth admissible forms g_σ with T(g_σ) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η.

Source: step 2(b) of the parent proof (Simon 7.2.4: (12), chapter-07.txt line 260; the bound before (13), lines 265–275; (13), line 276; and the subsequence-of-subsequence remark, lines 278–280). The current-specific input (the local comparison with the competitor S := C, converted to measures) is abstracted into hypothesis (b′); the remaining measure-theoretic argument is copied from the parent. No sibling result is used.
1. Fix a compact K and put L := limsup_j μ_j(K) ∈ [0, ∞].
2. (Claim: L ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) for every ε > 0.) Fix ε > 0 and suppose instead that a := μ(thickening(ε, K)) < L. Since [0, ∞] is densely ordered, choose b with a < b < L. Since b < limsup_j μ_j(K), μ_j(K) > b for infinitely many j (frequently in atTop; Mathlib frequently_lt_of_lt_limsup). Hence there is a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ with μ_{ψ(i)}(K) > b for all i (Mathlib Filter.extraction_of_frequently_atTop).
3. Apply (b′) to K, ε and ψ: there are W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ′ with limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W). By monotonicity of measures, μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≥ μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(K) > b for every i, so limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≥ b (Mathlib le_limsup_of_frequently_le). Also μ(W) ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) = a. Hence b ≤ limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W) ≤ a < b, a contradiction. This proves the claim.
4. (Continuity from above.) K is compact, hence closed. thickening(1, K) ⊆ cthickening(1, K), and cthickening(1, K) is compact (closed and bounded in ℝ^P; Mathlib IsCompact.cthickening), so μ(thickening(1, K)) ≤ μ(cthickening(1, K)) < ∞ by (a). The open sets thickening(r, K) decrease as r ↓ 0 and their intersection is closure K = K. By continuity of measure from above (Mathlib tendsto_measure_thickening_of_isClosed, which needs exactly one finite μ(thickening(R, K)) with R > 0 and K closed), μ(thickening(r, K)) → μ(K) as r → 0⁺.
5. By step 2, L ≤ μ(thickening(r, K)) for every r > 0. Since the right side tends to μ(K) as r → 0⁺ and the order interval [L, ∞] is closed, L ≤ μ(K). As K was arbitrary, the claim holds for every compact K. ∎
proof_key_steps: If μ(thickening(ε, K)) < b < limsup_j μ_j(K), extract a strictly increasing ψ with μ_{ψ(i)}(K) > b for all i.
Hypothesis (b′) along ψ gives W ⊇ K inside thickening(ε, K) and φ′ with limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W); monotonicity gives b ≤ limsup ≤ μ(W) ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) < b, a contradiction.
μ(thickening(1, K)) < ∞ by finiteness on the compact cthickening(1, K); continuity from above gives μ(thickening(r, K)) → μ(K) as r ↓ 0, hence limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K).

subproblems.title: The weak limit C is minimizing in ℝ^P (parent step 1; Simon 7.2.4 (8) and its localization)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For j ∈ ℕ let U_j ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), and let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity C). Assume (1) for every R ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U_j for all large j; (2) S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly: currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P)); (3) (local comparison) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, every ε > 0 and every strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ there are an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) = {x : infEdist(x, K) < ε} and a strictly increasing φ′ : ℕ → ℕ such that limsup_{i→∞} M_W(S_{ψ(φ′(i))}) ≤ M_W(S) for every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with SameBoundary S C (∂S = ∂C, vacuous for n = 0) and spt(S − C) ⊆ K. Then C is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ). That is, C is integer multiplicity, and M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S) whenever W ⊆ ℝ^P is open with compact closure, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity, SameBoundary S C holds, and spt(S − C) is compact and contained in W. Here M_O(T) = T.massOn O = sup{max(T(ω), 0) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(dom T), tsupport ω ⊆ O, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT massOn, Simon 6.2.5, Euclidean coefficient norm), spt is GeometricCurrentOn.support (Simon 6.2.11), and currentEval(S_j, ω) = S_j(ω) if ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ U_j and 0 otherwise.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (Simon 7.2.4, (8) and its localization: chapter-07.txt lines 226–229, with the comparison (12), line 260, and the lower semicontinuity of lines 262–263). Siblings used: mass_lsc (the parent's L3), mass_eq_measure (the parent's L2), mass_agree_off_support (the parent's use of V: S and C agree on forms supported in O = ℝ^P ∖ spt(S − C)), and measure_agree_on_borel with imrep_local_finiteness, which together with the previous two give the case U₁ = U₂ = ℝ^P, W := O of MEAS that the parent applies ('μ_S = μ_C on Borel subsets of O, in particular on W ∖ W′'). The argument is the parent's, step for step; only the appeal to MEAS is unfolded into these accepted components (MEAS is not available to a child of this node). Notation: M_G(T) = T.massOn G; all quantities lie in [0, ∞].
1. IsMinimizingIn C ℝ^P has two parts. The first, IsIntegerMultiplicity C, is a hypothesis. For the second, fix an open W with CompactlyContained W ℝ^P and an integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with SameBoundary S C such that K := spt(S − C) is compact and K ⊆ ℝ^P ∩ W = W. We must show M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S).
2. K is compact, W is open and K ⊆ W, so there is ε > 0 with thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open).
3. Apply hypothesis (3) with K, ε and ψ := id, which is strictly increasing. This gives an open W′ with K ⊆ W′ ⊆ thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W and a strictly increasing φ′ such that limsup_i M_{W′}(S_{φ′(i)}) ≤ M_{W′}(S′) for every integer multiplicity S′ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with SameBoundary S′ C and spt(S′ − C) ⊆ K. S itself qualifies, since spt(S − C) = K ⊆ K. Hence limsup_i M_{W′}(S_{φ′(i)}) ≤ M_{W′}(S).
4. By mass_lsc with φ := φ′ and O := W′: M_{W′}(C) ≤ liminf_i M_{W′}(S_{φ′(i)}) ≤ limsup_i M_{W′}(S_{φ′(i)}) ≤ M_{W′}(S). Here liminf ≤ limsup holds along atTop in the complete lattice [0, ∞].
5. Let R_C and R_S be integer multiplicity representations of C and S (they exist by IsIntegerMultiplicity C and IsIntegerMultiplicity S), and put μ_C := R_C.measure and μ_S := R_S.measure. By mass_eq_measure (U := ℝ^P, which is open), M_G(C) = μ_C(G) and M_G(S) = μ_S(G) for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P.
6. O := ℝ^P ∖ K is open, since K is compact and hence closed. Let G ⊆ O be open. Then G ∩ K = ∅ and spt(S − C) ⊆ K, so mass_agree_off_support (with U := ℝ^P, S := S, T := C, K := K, G := G) gives M_G(S) = M_G(C). By step 5, μ_S(G) = μ_C(G).
7. By imrep_local_finiteness (with U := ℝ^P and R := R_S), μ_S(K′) ≠ ∞ for every compact K′ ⊆ ℝ^P, in particular for every compact K′ ⊆ O. By measure_agree_on_borel (with O, μ := μ_S and ν := μ_C), using step 6 and this finiteness, μ_S(A) = μ_C(A) for every Borel set A ⊆ O.
8. W ∖ W′ is a Borel set (a difference of open sets) and W ∖ W′ ⊆ O because K ⊆ W′. By step 7, μ_S(W ∖ W′) = μ_C(W ∖ W′).
9. W′ ⊆ thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W and W′ is Borel, so μ(W) = μ(W′) + μ(W ∖ W′) for every measure μ on ℝ^P (Mathlib measure_inter_add_sdiff with W ∩ W′ = W′). Using steps 4, 5 and 8: M_W(C) = μ_C(W) = μ_C(W′) + μ_C(W ∖ W′) = M_{W′}(C) + μ_S(W ∖ W′) ≤ M_{W′}(S) + μ_S(W ∖ W′) = μ_S(W′) + μ_S(W ∖ W′) = μ_S(W) = M_W(S). These manipulations are valid in [0, ∞] without any finiteness assumption (addition is monotone in [0, ∞]).
10. Since W and S were arbitrary, C is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ). ∎
proof_key_steps: For a competitor S with K := spt(S − C) compact and ⊆ W, choose ε with thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W and apply the local comparison with ψ = id: an open W′ with K ⊆ W′ ⊆ W and φ′ with limsup_i M_{W′}(S_{φ′(i)}) ≤ M_{W′}(S).
mass_lsc along φ′ and liminf ≤ limsup give M_{W′}(C) ≤ M_{W′}(S).

mass_eq_measure turns masses on open sets into weights; mass_agree_off_support gives μ_S = μ_C on open subsets of O = ℝ^P ∖ K, and measure_agree_on_borel with imrep_local_finiteness extends this to Borel subsets of O, in particular W ∖ W′.
Additivity: μ_C(W) = μ_C(W′) + μ_C(W ∖ W′) ≤ μ_S(W′) + μ_S(W ∖ W′) = μ_S(W), i.e. M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S).

subproblems.title: Radon-criterion bounds for the mass measures: finiteness on compacts, compact lim sup, open lim inf (parent step 2(a)–(c); Simon 7.2.4 (12)–(14))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For j ∈ ℕ let U_j ⊆ ℝ^P be open and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), and let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). Assume (1) for every R ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U_j for all large j; (2) S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly); (3) (local comparison) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, every ε > 0 and every strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ there are an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) = {x : infEdist(x, K) < ε} and a strictly increasing φ′ : ℕ → ℕ such that limsup_{i→∞} M_W(S_{ψ(φ′(i))}) ≤ M_W(S) for every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with SameBoundary S C (∂S = ∂C, vacuous for n = 0) and spt(S − C) ⊆ K. Let R_j ∈ IMRep(U_j, n) represent S_j for every j, and let R ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, n) represent C. Write μ_j := R_j.measure = θ_j Hⁿ⌞M_j and μ := R.measure. Then (a) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; (b) limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; and (c) μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G) for every bounded open G ⊆ ℝ^P (lim sup and lim inf in [0, ∞]). These are exactly the hypotheses of radon_criterion for (μ_j) and μ. Here M_O(T) = T.massOn O = sup{max(T(ω), 0) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(dom T), tsupport ω ⊆ O, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT massOn, Simon 6.2.5, Euclidean coefficient norm), spt is GeometricCurrentOn.support (Simon 6.2.11), and currentEval(S_j, ω) = S_j(ω) if ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ U_j and 0 otherwise.

Source: step 2(a)–(c) of the parent proof (Simon 7.2.4 (12)–(14), chapter-07.txt lines 260–288, including the subsequence-of-subsequence remark of lines 278–280). Siblings used: mass_eq_measure (L2), mass_lsc (L3), limsup_criterion (LIM) and imrep_local_finiteness. The final application of radon_criterion stays in the selected parent node, where that result is a resolved dependency. Notation: M_G(T) = T.massOn G.
0. By mass_eq_measure: (i) M_G(C) = μ(G) for every open G, since ℝ^P is open and R represents C; (ii) M_G(S_j) = μ_j(G) for every open G and every j, since U_j is open and R_j represents S_j.
1. (a) Let K be compact. K ⊆ ℝ^P, so imrep_local_finiteness (with U := ℝ^P and R) gives μ(K) ≠ ∞, i.e. μ(K) < ∞. (This is the parent's computation μ(K) = ∫_{M_R ∩ K} θ_R dHⁿ < ∞ by locallyIntegrable_mult.)
2. (c) Let G be open; boundedness is not needed. By (i), mass_lsc with φ := id and O := G, and (ii) applied termwise: μ(G) = M_G(C) ≤ liminf_j M_G(S_j) = liminf_j μ_j(G).
3. (C is an admissible competitor for itself.) (α) C is integer multiplicity, witnessed by R. (β) SameBoundary C C: SameBoundary is defined by cases on the degree; for n = 0 it is True, and for n = m + 1 it is C.boundary = C.boundary, which holds by reflexivity. (γ) spt(C − C) = ∅. For every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), (C − C)(ω) = C(ω) − C(ω) = 0. Given x ∈ ℝ^P, the ball B := ball(x, 1) is open; its closure lies in the compact set closedBall(x, 1), so it is compact; closure B ⊆ ℝ^P; and C − C vanishes on every form supported in B. Thus B belongs to the family whose union is the zero region of C − C, and x ∈ B. So the zero region is ℝ^P and spt(C − C) = ℝ^P ∖ ℝ^P = ∅. In particular spt(C − C) ⊆ K for every K.
4. (b) We verify the hypotheses of LIM for the measures μ_j and μ. Its hypothesis (a) is step 1. For its hypothesis (b′), let K be compact, ε > 0 and ψ strictly increasing. Hypothesis (3) gives an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ′ such that limsup_i M_W(S_{ψ(φ′(i))}) ≤ M_W(S) for every admissible S. Taking S := C, admissible by step 3, gives limsup_i M_W(S_{ψ(φ′(i))}) ≤ M_W(C). W is open, so (ii) gives M_W(S_{ψ(φ′(i))}) = μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) for each i, and (i) gives M_W(C) = μ(W). So limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W), which is (b′) for this W and φ′. LIM now yields limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K.
5. Steps 1, 4 and 2 give the three conclusions (a), (b) and (c). ∎
